candidates.story: Trail of Bits critique of 1Password FLAWED patching benchmark
candidates.reason: Exact primary metadata and publisher RSS place the event inside the priority window. The critique supplies a consequential, non-duplicate evaluation dispute, public artifacts, independently authored underlying evidence and a concrete security-patch validation decision.

The cs.AI RSS event is exact and very fresh, but benchmark and human-collaboration findings are developer-produced, the preview uses broad promotional framing, and the discovery pass found no independent evaluation of the model or its 16-benchmark claims.

candidates.story: ActGuard pre-execution action auditing for indirect prompt injection
candidates.reason: The cs.AI/cs.CR RSS event is exact and code is linked, but security-utility results remain author-produced preprint evidence without independent reproduction; the theme also overlaps recent Index Us agent-security coverage.

The cross-list RSS timestamp is exact, but responsible automatic coverage needs a clinical-method audit of protected test material, synthetic-to-real overlap and judge validation before translating its high-stakes results into deployment advice.

candidates.story: On-premise medical AI agents for clinical decision-making

candidates.story: Recent Index Us coverage and corrections
candidates.reason: Current article bodies, source URLs and run records contain no coverage of FLAWED or the Trail of Bits critique and no correction target for this event. The recent native-harness article addresses a distinct same-model comparison and telemetry correction.

decision.reason: Trail of Bits published an exact-timestamped, non-duplicate critique that exposes why exploit blocking, complete repair and regression-free release cannot be collapsed into one AI-patching percentage. The underlying 1Password paper, released artifacts and NIST guidance support a practical local validation workflow while preserving both parties' evidence limits.

claims.text: Trail of Bits published the selected critique at 11:00 UTC on 15 September 2026.
The underlying 1Password report was published on 6 August 2026; the fresh event is the critique and related releases, not a new FLAWED experiment.
FLAWED reports 6,080 non-cheat classified patches across six selected vulnerabilities.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 overview; s4 Table 7 and target sections

claims.text: The study varied one-shot, iterative and exploratory modes; one-shot supplied no shell or test access, iterative supplied a reproducer, and exploratory allowed tools without the reproducer.
The nine prompt templates include two designed with wrong or incomplete fix guidance and others with no or correct guidance.
The study ran ChatGPT 5.5 at medium reasoning effort and Claude Opus 4.8 at high effort, described as defaults.
1Password reports a 26.0 per cent S1 clean-fix rate, defined as complete repair without unintended behaviour change.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 results; s4 Table 7 and S1 definition

claims.text: 1Password reports 20.1 per cent S2 patches and a 4.5 per cent S4+S5 new-vulnerability rate.
Trail of Bits says wrong-fix prompts account for 22 per cent of the data and no-build/no-test trials account for 36 per cent.
Trail of Bits filtered out trials without execution access, trials with deliberately wrong fix directions and runs flagged for consulting the upstream fix.
Trail of Bits reports that 2,634 of 3,067 filtered patches, or 86 per cent, blocked the supplied exploit.
Blocking the supplied exploit does not establish complete repair or freedom from regression.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 limitation after 86 per cent; s4 Sections 4.7 and 5

claims.text: The 26 per cent and 86 per cent figures cannot be treated as competing estimates of one success rate because both population and endpoint differ.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 S1/full design versus s1 filtered population/exploit endpoint

claims.text: The two model judges assigned different five-part outcomes to 36.8 per cent of the same patches.

Against human review, model verdict agreement was 65.9 per cent for the full grade and 87.7 per cent for original-bug closure across 1,052 cases, while new-bug agreement was 70.5 per cent across 1,059 cases.
The judge, rubric and human-adjudication sample are part of the result; averaging disagreeing judges does not create an objective correctness oracle.
Trail of Bits reports that maintainers merged 126 of 186 closed or merged Patch the Planet pull requests, with 91 merged submissions receiving no observed security-relevant revision.
Trail of Bits says maintainer acceptance does not establish correctness.
Trail of Bits reports reviewing about 33,500 later commits and finding functional, build/test/release and performance defects but no exploitable security vulnerability in that review.
Trail of Bits' operational data comes from agent patches directed and checked by its engineers and is not a matched independent comparison with FLAWED.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 operational method; s4 FLAWED design

claims.text: The post-patch-validation skill requires before/after reproduction, a distinct path, regression/security checks and an inconclusive outcome when the environment is broken.
The new post-patch-validation skill was not used in the Patch the Planet work described in the critique.
NIST SSDF recommends executable-code testing, tests for previously reported vulnerabilities, recorded results/issues and root-cause identification.
A local evaluation should retain separate evidence for exploit reproduction, alternate paths, regressions, new weaknesses, independent review and later release outcomes.
claims.sourceLocator: Synthesis; proposed workflow, not a measured guarantee

claims.text: Neither headline percentage is a universal deployment forecast; patching performance is conditional on sample, instructions, tools, model settings, judge and endpoint.
claims.sourceLocator: Synthesis of critique and study design

claims.text: The clean-fix rate varied sharply across the six selected vulnerabilities.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 critique sample-selection bullet reports 3-60 per cent; s4 Tables 8-10 provide per-vulnerability results

claims.text: The pinned FLAWED repository and published datasets expose the harness stages, sampling, grading, cross-validation and run artifacts for inspection.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 README pipeline, features, storage and datasets sections at pinned commit 2d3d15693b155873709bcf0daa247c2f0221d694

claims.text: 1Password recommends expert human review and local evaluation before AI-generated security patches are deployed.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 methodology, recommendations and final-thoughts sections
